policy.note: The plan starts at the safe end of the range plus a 25% cushion. Good check-ins move the date earlier. It never moves later; if recovery runs past it, the app sends you to a doctor.

safetyQuestion.question: Since yesterday, any new numbness or tingling, or a sudden jump in pain or swelling?

ankle.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Point your toes up and down and draw circles. How far does it move?
Can you stand on just the hurt foot for 30 seconds?

shoulder.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Can you lift your arm straight overhead?
Can you reach behind your back like tucking in a shirt?
Did it hurt while you were sleeping last night?

hamstring.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Lying on your stomach, bend your knee against light resistance. How does it feel?
Gently straighten your leg and lean forward a little. How does it feel?

wrist.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Can you bend your wrist up and down?
Can you grip a water bottle and twist the cap?
Can you put weight on your hand (push-up position)?

early: Ice wrapped in a towel for 20 minutes, a few times a day.
Keep your ankle raised above your heart when resting.
Wear a snug wrap or brace. Loosen it if your toes tingle or change color.
Use crutches if walking makes you limp.
later: Ice for 15-20 minutes after exercise if it gets sore.
Warm up with ankle circles before activity.
Wear a lace-up or semi-rigid brace for sports.

early: Ice wrapped in a towel for 20 minutes, a few times a day.
Sleep propped up, or with a pillow under your hurt arm.
No throwing, lifting, or reaching overhead for now.
later: A warm shower or heat pad before exercises can loosen it up.
Ice after exercise if it gets sore.
Keep your shoulders back, not hunched forward.

early: Ice wrapped in a towel for 20 minutes, a few times a day.
Skip heat for the first 2-3 days.
Don't stretch into pain. Gentle only.
Compression shorts or a wrap can help with swelling.
later: Heat or a warm shower before exercise, ice after if sore.
Gentle foam rolling on the muscle, not right on the sore spot.

early: Ice wrapped in a towel for 20 minutes, a few times a day.
Keep it raised and wrapped or braced.
Avoid catching, pushing, or carrying heavy things.
later: Warm water soaks before exercises can help it move.
Ice after activity if it gets sore.
Tape or brace it for sports until a doctor says otherwise.

relief.medicine: Talk to a parent, pharmacist, or doctor before taking any pain medicine.

places.label: Urgent care
places.when: Can't put weight on it, might need an X-ray, or swelling keeps getting worse.

places.label: Orthopedic walk-in
places.when: Bone and joint injuries. Many have walk-in hours.

places.label: Sports medicine doctor
places.when: Not getting better after a week, or it keeps getting hurt again.
